USDA Forest Service Sheyenne River Water Trail GeoPDF
providers.extractionMethod: Named hand-launch symbols extracted from the GeoPDF Sheyenne Canoe layer. Each feature coordinate uses the bottom-center anchor of the overlaid ESRI marker glyph, transformed through the GeoPDF LPTS/GPTS control points.

providers.name: Iowa DNR Boone County Des Moines River Water Trail and public water-access inventory
providers.extractionMethod: The official Boone County water-trail map identifies North Fraser and South Fraser as the concrete-ramp endpoints of the constructed portage around the Fraser low-head dam. Coordinates come from the matching Iowa DNR public water-access inventory features. Each inventory point was independently checked against current Esri World Imagery and coincides with the water-side end of the visible ramp, so it is retained as the water entry rather than projected to a mid-river flowline. North Fraser is visibly on the river even though the current NHD water polygon ends about 103 feet away; that known hydrography offset is preserved below.

providers.name: Iowa DNR North Raccoon River Water Trail and Sac County Grant Park ramp
providers.extractionMethod: The Iowa DNR water-trail guide identifies Grant Park as the take-out and portage for the Grant rock dam, and Sac County's park record independently confirms a hard-surface boat ramp on the North Raccoon River. The matching Iowa DNR public water-access inventory point (GlobalID a2d820d0-9ec9-4e4b-8525-9dc9717b1c10) was aligned with current Esri World Imagery; the water entry is the adjacent candidate-centered NHD river edge at the visible water-side end of that ramp, eight feet from the official access anchor. The farther route-centerline projection is intentionally rejected because it lies in mid-channel rather than at the ramp edge.

providers.name: Story County South Skunk River Water Trail and Lekwa Access ramp
providers.extractionMethod: Story County identifies Lekwa Access #242 at 56156 130th Street as a managed South Skunk River Water Trail access, and the official MyCountyParks record independently documents canoeing and kayaking with photographs of the signed access and its ramp reaching the river. The matching Iowa DNR public water-access inventory feature (GlobalID a39ce3e3-b29c-4f3b-8334-4f19ff04c40c) describes a concrete launch with six parking stalls and a 33-foot parking-to-access distance. Current Esri World Imagery places that inventory coordinate at the visible water-side ramp edge immediately south of the 130th Street bridge. It is retained as the water entry; the NHD and route-projected alternatives 23 and 50 feet farther east are rejected because they move into the channel.

providers.name: Wisconsin DNR Plum Creek Landing and Crawford County lower Kickapoo access
providers.extractionMethod: The Wisconsin DNR public-access inventory identifies feature 835 as Plum Creek Landing, a state-owned carry-in on the Kickapoo River, and Crawford County independently lists the Plum Creek/Kickapoo Wild Woods Canoe Landing. Wisconsin River Trips documents the exact Plum Creek-to-Highway-60 trip, while Miles Paddled's Plum-Creek-to-Wauzeka report publishes 43.11429, -90.91274 for this put-in and 43.08471, -90.87906 for the distinct Wauzeka take-out. Current Esri World Imagery places the DNR coordinate at the water-side edge of the visible gravel turnaround. Candidate-centered NHD evidence independently places it inside the river polygon and 18 feet from the Kickapoo flowline, so the exact DNR coordinate is retained as the water entry.

providers.name: Arkansas Game and Fish Commission Upper Illinois River Water Trail WOKA access pin
providers.extractionMethod: Decimal degrees decoded from the coordinate-linked WOKA Whitewater Park pin on the official AGFC Upper Illinois River Water Trail page. The published point is retained as the park/access anchor, not treated as the water entry; the official WOKA site map independently identifies a separate take-out ramp at the west end of the whitewater side channel.

providers.name: WOKA Whitewater Park official site map
providers.extractionMethod: The official WOKA site map labels TAKE OUT at the west roundabout and purpose-built ramp after Drop 8. The coordinate was derived by aligning that uniquely shaped roundabout/ramp with current satellite imagery and selecting the water-side end of the ramp. This is explicitly map-derived rather than a published coordinate and must also pass fresh candidate-centered NHD flowline and water-polygon checks.

providers.name: City of Columbus ADM river-access lease Exhibit A
providers.extractionMethod: The City of Columbus lease exhibit outlines the public access corridor from Southeast 9th Street to a unique sand-bank entry beside a wooded parcel. The exhibit is south-up; its rail line, canal, access road, wooded parcel, and braided-bank geometry were aligned to current satellite imagery before selecting the water-side end of the mapped corridor. Nebraska Game and Parks independently identifies this terminal access as lying on the Platte River about one mile downstream from the mouth of the Loup. Fresh candidate-centered NHD queries must verify the Platte River flowline, water polygon, and zero-gap Loup-Platte confluence topology before this map-derived point can be applied.

providers.name: Pennsylvania Fish and Boat Commission Susquehanna River Water Trail North Branch Section 4
providers.extractionMethod: Access coordinate transcribed from the official PFBC Section 4 river-access table and converted from whole-second DMS to decimal degrees. The table identifies Indian Head Campground as a ramp on river right at river mile 146.

providers.name: Endless Mountains Heritage Region Susquehanna River Water Trail North Branch 2021 Access Table
providers.extractionMethod: Decimal-degree access coordinates transcribed from pages 13-14 of the 2021 North Branch River Access & Services table. The table independently identifies launch type, river side, parking, and river mile. The published point is retained as the access anchor; the workflow derives the water-entry coordinate independently from candidate-centered NHD hydrography. These newer coordinates supersede the displaced whole-second DMS coordinates in the 2008 PFBC map series.

providers.name: Nebraska Game and Parks Commission State Lands
providers.extractionMethod: The coordinate is the representative/label point stored on the official George D. Syas WMA property polygon (PHA-NGPC-0000104 / 228W). It identifies the WMA as a whole; it is not a published launch, parking, or water-entry coordinate and must never be projected or auto-applied as one.

providers.name: Nebraska Game and Parks Commission Public Fishing Streams
providers.extractionMethod: The coordinate is the centroid recorded for the official George Syas WMA public-fishing stream polygon (PFA-0052), which covers a reach of the Loup River. It locates the fishable area, not a launch, parking area, or water-entry point, and must never be projected or auto-applied as one.

providers.name: North Dakota Game and Fish Department Lincoln Park boating access
providers.extractionMethod: The current North Dakota Game and Fish Department Fishing Facilities layer identifies ObjectID 1427 as an active, usable, 20-by-150-foot poured-concrete Red River boat ramp in the Lincoln Park/South Forks area, owned by the Grand Forks Park District. Its published GIS point lies on the upper portion of the visible ramp and is retained as the official facility anchor, not substituted for the water-entry coordinate.

providers.name: North Dakota Game and Fish Department and Minnesota DNR Lincoln Drive Park Landing
providers.extractionMethod: Minnesota DNR Red River State Water Trail Map 4 identifies Lincoln Drive Park Landing on the left/Grand Forks bank at river mile 304.1 as the trailer-access put-in for the official two-mile trip to LaFave Park. Visit Grand Forks independently directs users to the Lincoln Park boat ramp from Belmont Road and 13th Avenue South. The current North Dakota Game and Fish Department inventory identifies the matching active Grand Forks Park District poured-concrete ramp as ObjectID 1427 at 47.90888410499237, -97.02268528004571. Current Esri World Imagery shows that official point on the upper ramp; the coordinate below is the adjacent water-side end of the same visible concrete ramp, about 79 feet away. The distinct official facility anchor is preserved by provider ndgf_lincoln_drive_park_ramp_access_anchor.

providers.name: Minnesota DNR Central Park N public water access inventory
providers.extractionMethod: Minnesota DNR public-water-access record WAS02199 identifies Central Park N at river mile 13.8, administered by Anoka County, with a launch and one parking lot. The published GIS point is retained as the official facility/access anchor. The adjacent water-side slipway is represented separately by provider mn_dnr_rum_central_north_ramp_water_entry.

providers.name: Minnesota DNR and Anoka County Rum River Central Regional Park north ramp
providers.extractionMethod: Minnesota DNR Rum River Map 3 places the Central Regional Park trailer access, watercraft campsites, toilets, and drinking water at river mile 13.8. This uniquely selects the north facility: Minnesota public-water-access record WAS02199 is explicitly Central Park N at river mile 13.8, while the distinct Central Park S record WAS00323 is at river mile 10.7 near the map's fishing-pier/rest-area context. Anoka County's park page and summer map independently identify both a boat launch and canoe/kayak launch. The water-entry coordinate is the mapped slipway 8 feet from WAS02199; current Esri World Imagery aligns it with the north launch at the river edge.

providers.name: Nebraska Game and Parks Platte River State Park Decker Creek access
providers.extractionMethod: Nebraska Game and Parks identifies the canoe/kayak stop a few yards from the mouth of Decker Creek and publishes a photograph of the graded landing. Its Platte River Water Trail article gives the route topology: paddlers turn from the Platte up Decker Creek, pass under the railroad bridge, and reach the stop; the site was built as a river-accessible stop rather than a normal vehicle put-in/take-out, though boats may be wheeled down a maintenance road. The official photograph matches the uniquely shaped gravel landing, riprap, curved paved path, and footbridge visible in current Esri World Imagery. The coordinate is the water edge of that landing on the west bank of Decker Creek, immediately south of the footbridge.

providers.name: Nebraska Game and Parks Commission Loup River Water Trail Trip Planner
providers.extractionMethod: Decimal-degree start and end access-site coordinates transcribed from page 1 of the official Loup River Water Trail trip planner. The text identifies the Monroe Access Point as the public start, describes the downstream trip to Columbus, and publishes Start: 41.461082, -97.599121 / End: 41.418113, -97.367618. The coordinates are retained as access anchors rather than assumed water entries; the workflow derives water-entry coordinates independently from NHD hydrography. The accompanying page 2 map identifies water-access and parking symbols.

providers.name: National Park Service Tyler Bend upper launch parking area
providers.extractionMethod: The National Park Service identifies Tyler Bend as a primary boater access and describes the launch road connecting to its parking area. The NPS Tyler Bend area map places the boat launch on the upstream/west side of the bend. The facility coordinate is the center of the adjacent paved NPS parking footprint visible in current Esri World Imagery; it is retained separately from the water-entry coordinate.

providers.name: National Park Service Tyler Bend upper boat launch
providers.extractionMethod: The official NPS Tyler Bend area map marks the boat launch on the upstream/west side of the bend. The 2026 NPS concession operating plan removes the competing downstream feature from consideration by stating that only the Upper Tyler Bend access is available. The selected coordinate is the mapped upper gravel slipway, whose access road and shoreline landing align with current Esri World Imagery and the official map; the similarly named lower OSM slipway is not the currently authorized launch.

providers.name: City of Ann Arbor Gallup Park livery parking
providers.extractionMethod: The City of Ann Arbor ParkFocus web map identifies the Gallup Park parking lot serving the canoe-livery complex as ParkSymbols OBJECTID 755. The official parking coordinate is retained as the facility/access anchor and is intentionally separate from the Boat Dock water-entry feature.

providers.name: City of Ann Arbor Gallup Park livery Boat Dock
providers.extractionMethod: The current City of Ann Arbor ParkFocus amenities layer identifies Canoe Livery OBJECTID 288 and a distinct Boat Dock OBJECTID 351 at the livery shoreline. The City livery page independently describes an accessible launch, while the Huron River Water Trail identifies the Gallup Canoe Livery EZ Launch. The official dock point agrees within about 15 feet with the center of two mapped livery piers and is used as the water entry; the separate east-side trailer slipway is not substituted for this livery route endpoint.

providers.name: Arkansas Game and Fish Commission Rockhouse Access turnaround
providers.extractionMethod: AGFC states that its McIlroy Madison County WMA property joins the Kings River at Rockhouse Access, and The Nature Conservancy independently identifies Rockhouse as the AGFC-owned public access just upstream from the preserve. Kings River Arkansas describes a gravel road, ample parking, and a large gravel-bar launch near Rockhouse Creek. The facility anchor is the center of the unmistakable gravel turnaround connected to the independently mapped Rockhouse Boat Launch in current Esri World Imagery; it is stored separately from the shoreline water entry. This evidence class records official access identity plus transparent aerial derivation and is intentionally excluded from the unattended auto-apply source whitelist.

providers.name: Arkansas Game and Fish Commission Rockhouse gravel-bar water entry
providers.extractionMethod: AGFC and The Nature Conservancy establish the named site's public identity and ownership. Natural Atlas independently maps Rockhouse Boat Launch at 36.28193372205891, -93.6639968409015 and classifies it as a gravel launch on Rockhouse Creek and the Kings River. At that exact point, current Esri World Imagery visibly shows the gravel access road and turnaround terminating at the west bank; a candidate-specific National Map query places it about 107 feet from the Kings River NHD centerline. The older local route-guide coordinate is rejected because it lands about 0.8 mile south in forest. This evidence class is retained for expert-reviewed corrections but is not whitelisted for unattended auto-apply.

providers.name: Minnesota DNR Aqua Lane carry-in facility anchor
providers.extractionMethod: Minnesota DNR public-water-access record WAS02907 is the Anoka County Rice Lake carry-in off Aqua Lane at river mile 16.2. It documents one gravel carry-in ramp, one five-car parking lot, and the downstream-left bank. The heads-up-digitized GIS point is retained as the official facility/access anchor; the adjacent shoreline water entry is recorded separately by provider anoka_rice_creek_aqua_lane_water_entry.

providers.name: Anoka County Rice Creek Water Trail Aqua Lane carry-in
providers.extractionMethod: The current Anoka County/RCWD Rice Creek Water Trail map places the Aqua Lane access immediately upstream of the road crossing, with limited parking east of the channel. Minnesota DNR public-water-access record WAS02907 independently identifies the same Anoka County carry-in, specifies one gravel carry-in ramp and five-car parking, and records the access on the downstream-left bank at river mile 16.2. Because its heads-up-digitized GIS point falls at the bridge/facility rather than a shoreline edge, the water entry below is derived separately at the east-bank water edge visible immediately upstream of the bridge in current Esri World Imagery. The DNR feature remains the distinct authoritative facility anchor.

providers.name: Ramsey County Long Lake Boat Landing parking anchor
providers.extractionMethod: Ramsey County's Long Lake Regional Park map identifies the south-shore boat launch and its dedicated parking area. Minnesota DNR record WAS01204 independently documents one asphalt lot with 15 car and 11 trailer spaces at the same facility. The coordinate is the center of that unmistakable paved launch lot in current Esri World Imagery and is retained separately from the GPS-mapped concrete water entry.

providers.name: Minnesota DNR Long Lake Boat Landing water entry
providers.extractionMethod: Minnesota DNR public-water-access record WAS01204 identifies the GPS-collected south-shore Long Lake facility, administered by Ramsey County, with two concrete-slab ramps, one dock, and trailer parking. Its official coordinate lands directly on the visible concrete slipway and is about 15 feet from the independently mapped OSM slipway. The Anoka County/RCWD water-trail map identifies this exact Long Lake Boat Landing as the 15.2-mile full-route finish, distinct from the limited canoe access at Long Lake Beach farther north. The DNR GPS coordinate is therefore retained as the water entry rather than projected to the distant Rice Creek centerline.
